observable_outcome: The persisted record envelope is read against an accepted set of record schema versions instead of one exact string, through a single predicate that all five read-side refusal sites in internal/store/firestore call -- DecodeRecord, decodeDocument, the outbox scan and the two bounded collection scans. The written value stays exactly what it is today and is pinned by a test that names what it pins, so a bump cannot ride along with the widening. A test-only substitution of the accepted set proves a second envelope id is read by all five paths and a third is refused by all five, and a non-native envelope id is additionally refused when its payload does not satisfy the domain validity predicate, so nothing whose payload the running code cannot interpret is accepted silently. The memory adapter is proven to have no second envelope implementation to disagree with.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written before any code. The evidence opens with a table with one row per stage in docs/operations/self-update.md section 7.1 -- expand, coexist, migrate, contract -- stating for each what this task does, what it deliberately does not, and who owns the remainder. The expand row is the only one with work in it. The coexist row must state that it depends on V2-069's Runner version report to be observable. The migrate row must state that no backfill, cursor or tick is added. The contract row must state that the section 7.2 predicate, which is the same predicate as GC eligibility in section 8, is not implemented. A further row must state that this task blocks M8 completion condition 3 and does not satisfy it. Nothing in the evidence may claim any release gate.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. Record the top-level test names and counts of internal/store/firestore (9: six in store_test.go and three in quota_integration_test.go) and internal/store/memory (4), and that all pass. Record the complete measured envelope map with line numbers: const RecordSchema at store.go:31; write sites at store.go:68 (EncodeRecord), store.go:127 (encodeDocument) and client.go:59 (installation record); the document struct field at store.go:89; and the five read-side refusal sites at store.go:79, :173, :1230, :1348 and :1484. Record explicitly that docs/operations/self-update.md section 7.3 names only two of those five, and that the other three are on scan paths. Record that the payload decode is a plain json.Unmarshal at store.go:81-83 and :175-177 and that no validity predicate is called on read today. Record that internal/store/memory has no envelope at all, with the argv used to establish it. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged, and before/after top-level counts per touched package must be reported.

A3. One accepted set, one predicate. Add AcceptedRecordSchemas as an ordered, closed, duplicate-free declaration and RecordSchemaAccepted(string) bool, and convert all five read-side sites to call the predicate. Assert that the shipped set has exactly one member and that the member is the value the encode paths write. Assert the predicate uses exact string equality: a table asserts refusal for a prefix of an accepted id, a suffix of one, a case variant, a leading-space variant, a trailing-space variant and the empty string. No normalization, trimming or case folding may be introduced.

A4. All five sites, proven by behaviour and not by inspection. With the accepted set substituted in a test to two members and restored via defer, assert that a document written under the second id is read successfully through every one of the five paths: DecodeRecord, decodeDocument, the outbox scan at store.go:1230, and the two bounded collection scans at store.go:1348 and :1484. With the same substitution, assert that a document under a third id is refused with ErrInvalidSchema through every one of the five. Name in the evidence which concrete store operation exercises each of the five sites, and record the argv of the run that proves it. The production accepted set must not be widened to make any of this pass.

A5. The written value is pinned so a bump announces itself. Add a test whose name states that it pins the written envelope value, asserting: the written value equals a literal string in the test body; AcceptedRecordSchemas contains the written value; every member matches a declared id shape; and the set has no duplicates. Assert that a store cannot write a value it would refuse to read, by round-tripping every member of the accepted set through the encode and decode paths.

A6. Payload interpretability for non-native ids. Under the test-only two-member substitution, assert that a document carrying a non-native accepted envelope id is refused with ErrInvalidSchema when its payload does not satisfy the domain validity predicate for its kind -- at minimum an empty requirement id, an unknown requirement status, and a payload that is valid JSON of the wrong shape -- and accepted when it does. Assert that for the native id the decode path is unchanged: run the pre-existing store tests and record that no assertion, error value or status changed, and assert explicitly that no validity predicate is invoked on the native path.

A7. No refusal is weakened. For each of the five sites assert that all four existing refusal reasons still refuse: malformed JSON or a DataTo failure, an envelope id outside the accepted set, a kind mismatch, and an empty payload or value. TestCodecRejectsCorruption keeps its three existing inputs at store_test.go:70 unchanged and passing under its own name; add the near-miss cases from A3 as new cases in a new test rather than by editing that table.

A8. The five sites are the complete set, proven by a source scan. Add internal/store/firestore/source_guard_test.go modelled on internal/domain/source_guard_test.go: parse every *.go file in the package with go/parser, fail outright on a zero-file scan, assert the RecordSchema declaration was actually found, and assert the identifier appears in a non-test file only in its own declaration, in the accepted-set declaration, in the predicate and in the three write sites -- and nowhere in a read-side comparison outside the predicate. Verify the matcher first against a known-positive fixture source containing a synthesized comparison and a known-negative without one; record both control results.

A9. The memory adapter has no second envelope. Add internal/store/memory/source_guard_test.go asserting by AST and literal scan, failing outright on a zero-file scan, that no struct field, constant or string literal named or valued record_schema exists in the package, and record the argv. Do not edit internal/store/memory/store.go or its existing test file. Record in the evidence that this is what makes the both-stores requirement checkable: there is exactly one envelope implementation in the repository, and the memory adapter has none to disagree with.

A10. Scan failure semantics, asserted deliberately. Assert and record that a document failing the envelope or payload check inside a bounded scan fails the whole scan with ErrInvalidSchema rather than being skipped, at each of store.go:1230, :1348 and :1484. Do not introduce partial-scan or skip-the-bad-document semantics; that would be a new failure contract this task has no mandate to create. State the consequence in the documentation.

A11. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every wait is a bounded deadline poll and every timestamp comes from an injected clock. Run devbox run --pure -- make component-store-firestore three times in sequence and record that the verdict line is identical each time. The Firestore assertions run through the emulator scripts/firestore-emulator.sh starts; if the emulator is unavailable, record the affected checks as skipped with their reason and never count a skip as a pass (gate rule G7).

A12. Measured notes for V2-045, recorded and not acted on. Record that this task creates no new import edge: store-firestore already declares [application, domain, infra, runner] and already imports internal/domain, and store-memory gains a test file only. Record that it moves the store-firestore, store-memory and docs component keys. V2-045 has landed, so internal/ci's manifest check will turn make check red if the declared component dependencies and the real import graph diverge: because this design creates no edge, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from -- stop and escalate to the tech_lead and do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.* to make it green.

A13. Documentation. Create docs/operations/record-envelope.md describing: the envelope shape and the complete map of write sites and read sites with the count, stating that section 7.3 measured two of five; the accepted set, the predicate, and the fact that the shipped set has one member because this is the expand stage; why exact membership and no normalization; the payload-interpretability gate for non-native ids and why it does not apply to the native id; the scan failure semantics from A10; that the memory adapter has no envelope and the guard that keeps that true; and the sequencing rule that a bump is a separate Increment, naming the test that enforces it. Do not edit docs/operations/self-update.md or any other document.

A14. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-070-store-firestore.json (id ev-v2-070-store-firestore, task_id V2-070, component store-firestore, correlation_id v2-070-envelope-expand) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-070-store-memory.json (id ev-v2-070-store-memory, task_id V2-070, component store-memory, same correlation_id), recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, with every acceptance item traceable to a named check. Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and never counted as a pass. Register both with exactly two appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place. Any digest written in prose must match the .gitleaks.toml allowlist shape (64 or 40 hex characters, at most one trailing punctuation character).

A15. Component evidence keys. The evidence_key recorded in each artifact is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added: a new file that is not yet in the index is invisible to the git ls-files based input set that key is derived from.

A16. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs and judge them by the verdict line, not by the shell exit status. No file outside allowed_paths changes.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.
Do not bump the written envelope value in this change. The shipped accepted set has exactly one member, the value the encode paths already write, and the pinning test must fail if that value changes.
Do not widen the production accepted set to make a test pass. The second and third envelope ids exist only inside a test that substitutes the set and restores it via defer.
Do not weaken any refusal. Membership is exact string equality; no trimming, case folding, prefix matching or normalization of any kind may be introduced.

Do not apply the payload validity predicate to the native envelope id. Today's read path must be unchanged byte for byte, so that every existing store test keeps passing under its own name with its own assertions.
Do not introduce partial-scan or skip-the-bad-document semantics in the three scan sites. A failing document fails the scan, as it does today.

Do not touch internal/domain, internal/application, internal/api, internal/web, contracts/openapi/** or internal/store/memory/store.go. This task is deliberately outside the surface-widening chain and must stay there.
Do not start a migrate or contract stage: no backfill, no cursor, no tick, no deletion of any field, and no implementation of the section 7.2 or section 8 predicate.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. This design creates no new import edge, so a red manifest or dependency-coverage check in make check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than editing any of those files.
Do not edit contracts/release-contract/** and do not weaken any capability declaration there.
Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, any .agents/v2/packets/** file, or .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**.
Do not edit docs/operations/self-update.md; V2-034 and V2-035 own it and a concurrent edit produces a conflict whose resolution is worse than a new document.
Do not touch any Google Cloud resource. The Firestore assertions run through the local emulator path scripts/firestore-emulator.sh already provides for make component-store-firestore.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is bounded deadline polling, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip with status skipped and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.

Do not claim, in any record or document, that this task satisfies M8 completion condition 3 or any part of the coexist, migrate or contract stages. It supplies the expand stage only, and behaviour is unchanged today; say so.
